header: Date: 2025-07-21 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Alex Nguyen (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Martin Cole (CTO, Evercrest), Priya Sharma (Lead ML Eng, Evercrest), Dana Ruiz (Head of Product, Evercrest)
summary: Intro call to evaluate Redwood's hosted vs reserved/dedicated vs private deployments focusing on fast time-to-first-token (TTFT) for a customer-facing product. Discussed self-serve/plg quickstart credits, security requirements (SSO/KMS/SOC2), sample workload characteristics, and next steps for a hosted pilot with benchmarking. Customer inclined to start with hosted credits to move quickly but has enterprise constraints that may lead to a Private deployment later.
topics: Introductions; current stack & infra; TTFT/first-call goals; hosted credits quickstart flow; dedicated/reserved vs private tradeoffs; security & compliance (SOC2, KMS, SSO); performance expectations (latency/QPS); billing/credits; pilot scope and timings; next steps and owners.
references: Security pack (SOC2 summary, encryption/KMS brief) — to be attached by SE
Pilot runbook template: shared in chat
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Nguyen: Alright everyone can hear me? Good afternoon. Thanks for joining, we'll run about 40 minutes. Alex from Redwood, with Sofia our solutions engineer.
[00:07] Martin Cole: Yup, hear you. Thanks Alex. Appreciate you fitting this in.
[00:12] Alex Nguyen: Awesome. High level, we want to understand your goals for time-to-first-token and which path — quick hosted credits vs reserved capacity vs a private deployment. Can you give a bit of context on the product?
[00:24] Dana Ruiz: Yeah sure — so Evercrest runs a chat-assist feature inside our commerce platform, real-time suggestions and summarization for support agents. We're looking to replace internal LLM infra 'cause cost/ops are heavy. Main ask is fast prototype to push to a small set of users in 2–3 weeks.
[00:40] Priya Sharma: From ML side we also need to validate latency under real load. Typical prompt riff is 120–300 tokens input, responses ~60–120 tokens, peak qps estimated 30–50 for pilot but could burst. We also have PII so data handling is a concern.
[00:58] Sofia Patel: Got it. Hosted quickstart usually maps well to that. We give credits to run a pilot, quick API keys, and can stream responses. There's an onboarding flow that gets you to first token in hours if you have your dataset and prompt ready.
[01:12] Martin Cole: Hours sounds great. But security — we need SOC2, SSO, and ability to ship logs to our SIEM. Also key management — we prefer KMS integration.
[01:24] Sofia Patel: Totally; on the hosted side we provide SOC2 reports, and we support sending audit logs to your retention endpoint. For KMS we have customer-managed key options on Private; hosted can do envelope encryption and we can discuss enterprise KMS integrations if needed.
[01:38] Dana Ruiz: So hosted is fine for the pilot, but long-term we might do private because of regulatory needs in EU.
[01:47] Alex Nguyen: That's a common pattern. Start hosted to validate TTFT and user experience, then evaluate Dedicated or Private for residency and KMS. For TTFT specifically — can you define what metric you care about? Median latency to first token, or tail p95, or the total end-to-end response time?
[02:02] Priya Sharma: We care about p95 < 600ms for first token ideally, median 200–300. For the pilot that's acceptable. Also cost per 1k tokens matters but not as much as latency for agent UX.
[02:16] Sofia Patel: Ok, initial note — if you're using a smaller open model we can hit those numbers hosted, but model choice and quantization matter. We typically recommend a balanced model for low latency and cost. We also have streaming so front-end can render token-by-token and feel snappy even if full generation takes slightly longer.
[02:34] Martin Cole: Can you elaborate on the variance? How does Dedicated change latency vs hosted?
[02:40] Sofia Patel: Dedicated reserves GPU pools for your tenancy which flattens cold start variance and concurrency contention. Hosted works well and is multi-tenant but if you need absolute predictability at high qps, Dedicated is better. Private adds full network isolation and lets you plug in your KMS.
[02:55] Dana Ruiz: For the pilot do we need to setup any infra? We want to avoid VPNs or long network onboarding.
[03:02] Alex Nguyen: No for hosted quickstart you just need an API key and allowlist IP or standard auth — we can handle most of it without VPN. We also have a browser-based playground and SDKs to speed things.
[03:12] Priya Sharma: Regarding data retention — can you confirm hosted doesn't retain PII by default? We need clear terms.
[03:18] Sofia Patel: By default logs for debugging are kept for a short retention; enterprise retention and data deletion policies can be arranged. We'll share the security pack that spells this out, including deletion timelines.
[03:30] Martin Cole: Cool. Pricing — credits are fine for pilot. How many credits do you give? What's typical TTFT cost for 2–3 weeks of testing at our qps?
[03:40] Alex Nguyen: We usually give a 30–60k token credit for early pilots — enough for a couple thousand sessions. For your workload, rough back-of-envelope: if each session is 400 tokens total and you run 5k sessions, that's 2M tokens; we'll do a more accurate estimate once Priya shares sample traffic. We'll include a sample cost table in the email.
[04:02] Dana Ruiz: We should schedule the benchmark run — maybe next week?
[04:06] Sofia Patel: Yes, we can run a benchmark with a small dataset. We'll do a 1-hour throughput session to show median and p95 first-token times and a latency/cost tradeoff with model variants.
[04:18] Priya Sharma: One technical thing — we heavily rely on KV cache for conversational context. Can Redwood do prefix/KV caching and what are cache-hit implications on latency?
[04:28] Sofia Patel: Yes, the runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching to reduce repeated computation. Hit rate improves effective latency significantly for multi-turn; we'll include recommendations on batching and cache sizing. Sometimes transcriptions show "K V cash" — but it's KV cache (memory of past tokens).
[04:44] Martin Cole: Any gotchas with our cloud provider? We're on GCP (us-west1) but have a chunk of infra in AWS.
[04:52] Alex Nguyen: We support region-based routing. For hosted we can route to closest region; for Private you can deploy in your VPC on GCP. We'll need some network details for firewall rules for Private later.
[05:03] Dana Ruiz: For the POC, who will own configuration? Our SRE or Redwood?
[05:09] Sofia Patel: For hosted pilot Redwood manages runtime; we'll provide the configuration suggestions and can do some managed runs. For Dedicated or Private the operations hand-off is clarified in the runbook.
[05:20] Priya Sharma: What telemetry do you expose? We want token-level cost, per-route latency, and trace IDs to wire into our tracing.
[05:28] Sofia Patel: We expose per-request metadata, token counts, model id, and per-route dashboards. You can also stream traces to your tracing backend via our tracing hooks. We'll share a sample dashboard.
[05:40] Martin Cole: Competitors — any reason to pick Redwood vs Anthropic or OpenAI for this use-case?
[05:46] Alex Nguyen: Our focus is production inference economics — transparent benchmarks and operational tools for rollouts. We also support a consistent interface across hosted/dedicated/private which helps if you start hosted and want to move into Private later without changing code. We typically show customers cost/latency tradeoff comparisons as part of the pilot.
[06:02] Dana Ruiz: Great. Are there any immediate blockers to getting started?
[06:07] Alex Nguyen: For the hosted pilot: need a single API key, a contact for SSO (if you want playground SSO), sample inference traces from Priya, and confirmation to provision credits. For Private you'd need additional network contacts.
[06:20] Priya Sharma: I'll export sample trace logs and a small set of representative prompts. Expect that by EOD Thursday.
[06:27] Martin Cole: I'll get SRE contact to you.
[06:30] Alex Nguyen: Perfect. We'll send a pilot proposal doc after this call with the suggested credit amount and dates. We'll also attach our security pack.
[06:38] Dana Ruiz: One last question about rollback and fallbacks — if you lose Dedicated capacity do you failover to hosted?
[06:44] Sofia Patel: Yes — we have routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. For critical services we recommend defining fallback tiers and A/B canary rollouts.
[06:55] Priya Sharma: Also curious about quantization — do you do 4-bit quantization MQA for cost reduction?
[07:02] Sofia Patel: We have quantization-friendly execution paths in the runtime and recommend specific quantized model variants. We'll include recommended quant profiles in the runbook.
[07:12] Martin Cole: Thanks. Anything else?
[07:15] Alex Nguyen: That's the bulk. We'll follow up with pricing, security docs, and a proposed pilot start date. Recommended next meeting: bench run week of 2025-07-28.
[07:26] Dana Ruiz: Sounds good. Thank you.
[07:28] Alex Nguyen: Thanks everyone. We'll email the items and get the pilot provisioned once Priya and Martin send the artifacts.
[07:35] [call ends]
